title: 2026 Florida U.S. Senate special election
description: Florida’s 2026 special U.S. Senate election will fill the remainder of Marco Rubio’s term, with a general election on November 3, 2026 and primaries on August 18, 2026. Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed Republican Ashley Moody to the seat after Rubio left for the Trump administration, and the winner will serve the final two years of the term Rubio won in 2022. The race is a partisan test in a state that has trended more Republican in recent cycles, with Democrats trying to make the contest competitive despite the GOP’s statewide advantage. The main contrast is between Moody’s statewide record and fundraising strength and Democrats’ effort to find a nominee with enough name recognition and crossover appeal to challenge her.

Healthcare.stance: Moody has focused on health-care fraud enforcement, including legislation to crack down on Medicaid fraud and calls to recover allegedly improper ACA subsidy payments. She has also opposed extending ACA premium subsidies.

Economy.stance: Moody says she supports cutting burdensome regulations, lowering taxes, expanding domestic energy production, and bringing manufacturing back to the U.S. Her campaign also highlights housing affordability and support for Florida agriculture as part of her economic agenda.

Climate/Energy.stance: Moody’s campaign emphasizes expanding domestic energy production, including oil, gas, nuclear, and newer technologies, as part of an energy-independence agenda. She has also backed legislation aimed at helping Florida agriculture adapt to extreme weather.

Reproductive Rights.stance: Moody has taken a pro-life position and sponsored legislation to require parental notification before a minor crosses state lines for an abortion. Her public messaging emphasizes parental rights and accountability in abortion-related cases.

Immigration.stance: Moody supports stricter immigration enforcement, including finishing the border wall, ending sanctuary-city policies, and speeding removal of people she describes as illegal or criminal aliens. She has introduced legislation to expand state enforcement and accelerate removals.

Guns & Safety.stance: Moody says she supports gun rights and has opposed federal gun-control measures she describes as overreach. She joined litigation against a Biden administration rule expanding background-check requirements at gun shows.

Foreign Policy.stance: Moody’s campaign says she favors a strong military, border security, reduced foreign aid that does not serve U.S. interests, and less support for international bodies she views as misaligned with American priorities. Her campaign also emphasizes U.S. leadership in space and American sovereignty.

Social Justice.stance: Moody’s public messaging centers on law enforcement, border security, and tougher criminal enforcement rather than social-justice reforms. I did not find a detailed campaign platform outlining broader civil-rights or social-justice proposals.

candidates.name: Alexander Vindman
candidates.summary: Alexander Vindman is a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel and former National Security Council official running as a Democrat in Florida’s 2026 special U.S. Senate election. His campaign centers on affordability, anti-corruption messaging, and his background as a national security whistleblower during President Donald Trump’s first impeachment.

reviews.summary: This profile is well-researched, well-sourced, and internally consistent across both major candidates. Ashley Moody's extensive issue positions are backed by official Senate sources, campaign pages, and credible news outlets with high confidence across all 12 issue areas. Alexander Vindman's more limited public record is handled honestly—low-confidence stances are clearly marked as 'no public position found' rather than fabricated. Career histories for both candidates are detailed and consistent with their cited sources. The polling data is current (Feb–Mar 2026) and properly attributed. Language is neutral throughout, with no evident partisan bias in framing or word choice. The only minor gaps—Vindman's lack of detailed positions on climate, reproductive rights, and education—are documented as genuine absences of public statements, not research failures. Generator metadata is correctly formatted. A strong, professional profile suitable for public use.

High-confidence stances backed by multiple primary sources; low-confidence issues transparently documented.
